tasks.title: TASK 0: Initialize Convex in Next.js Frontend
tasks.description: Set up foundational Convex client integration with WorkOS AuthKit in the Next.js frontend to establish the foundation for all backend functionality. This is the essential first task that must be completed before any other Convex integration work can begin.
tasks.details: 1. Install required packages: `npm install convex @convex-dev/auth` 2. Initialize Convex project with `npx convex dev` and configure convex.json with proper deployment settings 3. Set up environment variables for CONVEX_URL and NEXT_PUBLIC_CONVEX_URL in .env.local 4. Create convex/ directory structure with schema.ts, auth.config.ts, and initial function files 5. Replace the existing mock authentication context in src/hooks/useOrganization.tsx with Convex auth hooks 6. Create app layout wrapper using ConvexProviderWithAuthKit, integrating WorkOS AuthKit configuration 7. Update all components currently using mock auth to use Convex auth state 8. Configure WorkOS integration in convex/auth.config.ts with proper domain and client ID settings 9. Test that frontend successfully connects to Convex development server and auth flow works
tasks.testStrategy: 1. Verify `npm run dev` starts without errors and Convex provider initializes 2. Test that `npx convex dev` connects successfully and shows deployment URL 3. Confirm authentication state persists across page reloads using Convex auth hooks 4. Test login/logout flow works with WorkOS AuthKit integration 5. Verify environment variables are properly configured and accessible 6. Check that all existing mock auth-dependent components render without errors 7. Validate that Convex client can execute basic queries/mutations 8. Test that auth context provides expected user data structure matching existing types
